text:
Alex K: quick question about flag resolution order — we hit a weird case where a model-level toggle was unexpectedly taking effect even though project-level override exists. can someone confirm precedence?

Tara S: generally we expect precedence: route -> model -> project -> org (most specific wins). but there are exceptions with wildcard routes and explicit 'force' tags.

Mohan P: @Tara can you expand on the wildcard bit? the failing scenario: route `search/*` has no explicit flag, project sets `feature_x: off`, model sets `feature_x: on`. which should win?

Tara S: with `search/*` the runtime tries route match first. if no explicit route entry, it looks for a route-level audience match (canary). if none, it falls back to model. so in your case model:on would win unless project has an explicit `inherit: false` or `force: project` setting.

Jen L: fwiw we had a request from product to ensure project-level perf flags can always force off for safety. is that `force` field something teams can set?

Alex K: yes, product wants safety guardrails — how would we express that in config? can we show a minimal example?

Mohan P: here's what I prototyped in the flag catalog JSON: 
```json
{"scope": {
  "org": null,
  "project": {"force": "project", "value": "off"},
  "model": {"value": "on"}
}
}
```
If `force` is present at project scope it short-circuits the search and enforces project value.

Tara S: caution: `force` is powerful. we should limit to org- or project-admins and require a changelog entry + 24h alert when used.

flag-bot: note: audit log entry created for flag change by Mohan P (cfg-id: fk-9932).

Jen L: sounds reasonable. are there any existing routes for canary audiences that could cause unexpected model wins? e.g., if a route has an audience but the model is annotated for a different audience set.

Mohan P: yes — audience evaluation order matters. current order: route audience -> route percent rollout -> model audience -> project default. so if a route has audience A but the model has audience B, and user matches B but not A, model will enable. that's intended but surprising to PMs.

Alex K: proposal: document this in rollout guardrails and add an optional `audience-strictness` flag on routes (`strict|lenient`) where `strict` mandates route audience be the only one considered. defaults to `lenient`.

Tara S: +1. add a linting rule: if a route defines a canary audience and model also defines one, warn unless route sets `audience-strictness`. this will prevent silent model takeovers.

Jen L: can we add a short checklist for on-call when flipping `force` or `audience-strictness`? e.g., notify #incidents, post rollout note, enable quick rollback route.

Alex K: good call. action items: 1) Mohan to open a small RFC PR for `force` behaviour + example (ETA 1d) 2) Tara to add lint rule and flag-bot audit enforcement (ETA 2d) 3) Jen to draft PM-facing docs + checklist (ETA 2d)

Mohan P: will do the RFC. pinging reviewers: @Tara S and @Alex K.

Tara S: also adding automated alert when `force` is set for >1hr. prevents accidental permanent overrides.

flag-bot: reminder: add tests that simulate wildcard route fallthrough to model-level flags.

Alex K: thanks everyone. I'll follow up in the RFC PR thread. :thumbsup:
